sql:
SELECT z.Borough, COUNT(*) AS touches
FROM lake.trips t
JOIN ops.zones z ON z.LocationID = t.PULocationID OR z.LocationID = t.DOLocationID
GROUP BY z.Borough
ORDER BY z.Borough

diagnosis.bottleneck: The BLOCKWISE_NL_JOIN (node 8) performs a nested-loop join over 495,833 trips rows and 265 zones rows with an OR join condition (PULocationID OR DOLocationID), preventing hash-join optimization and likely executing ~130M comparisons.

plan_nodes.note: Join Type: INNER | Condition: ((LocationID = CAST(PULocationID AS BIGINT)) OR (LocationID = CAST(DOLocationID AS BIGINT)

hypotheses.claim: An OR inside the JOIN condition cannot use a hash join; the engine falls back to a nested-loop style join, which is far more expensive than two equi-joins. (matched: inner join ops.zones z on z.locationid = t.pulocationid or z.locationid = t.dolocationid)

The OR join condition forces a nested-loop join instead of a hash join; rewriting as a UNION ALL of two separate equi-joins (one on PULocationID, one on DOLocationID) followed by aggregation would enable hash joins and reduce comparisons to ~1M.
Neither trips.PULocationID nor trips.DOLocationID has an index; creating a hash index or sorting trips on both columns would allow a merge join or hash join on each key individually.
The blockwise nested-loop join materializes the full cross-product for the OR condition; pushing a bloom filter or pre-filtering zones into the scan could reduce the inner-loop iterations.
